camps.name: Upper Royal Basin
camps.why: Camping at the upper tarns cuts about a mile and 500 feet from each end of summit day and puts the Johnson-Clark notch above your tent. Needs an upper-basin permit.

camps.name: Royal Lake
camps.why: Designated, reservable sites with toilets one mile lower; pick it when upper-basin permits are gone and accept a longer summit day.

plan_conflict: Upper Royal Basin and Royal Lake both carry main on file; research puts most climbing parties at the upper basin tarns, so Royal Lake is changed to route.

camps.name: Upper Royal Basin
camps.why: Closest camp to Royal Pass and Deception Basin, about an hour from the pass, so the snowfield, glacier crossing and class 3 finish fit one day from your tent.

camps.name: Royal Lake
camps.why: Designated lake sites with toilets and an easier permit; adds roughly a mile and 500 feet each way to the Mystery day, so choose it when the upper basin is full.

plan_conflict: Upper Royal Basin and Royal Lake both carry main on file; research puts most climbing parties at the upper basin tarns, so Royal Lake is changed to route.

camps.name: Upper Royal Basin
camps.why: Sleeping at the foot of the Needles' east wall saves about a mile and 500 feet each way on the ridge-scramble day. Needs an upper-basin permit, taken by phone.

camps.name: Royal Lake
camps.why: The designated lake camp the park lists, with toilets and reservable sites; adds a mile of approach each end of the ridge day.

plan_conflict: Upper Royal Basin and Royal Lake both carry main on file; research puts most climbing parties at the upper basin tarns, so Royal Lake is changed to route. The plan says Royal Lake and that Upper Royal Basin is closed to camping, but the park page lists only Royal Lake sites while climbers' reports show upper-basin camping on a phone permit.

camps.name: Upper Royal Basin
camps.why: Puts the talus below Sundial's east face minutes from camp, so the Class 3 climb is a short half day. Needs an upper-basin permit, taken by phone.

camps.name: Royal Lake
camps.why: The designated lake camp the park lists, with toilets and reservable sites; adds about a mile and 500 feet each way to the Sundial day.

plan_conflict: Upper Royal Basin and Royal Lake both carry main on file; research puts most climbing parties at the upper basin tarns, so Royal Lake is changed to route. The plan says Royal Lake and that Upper Royal Basin is closed to camping, but the park page lists only Royal Lake sites while climbers' reports show upper-basin camping on a phone permit.

camps.name: Nine Stream — last low camp before the First Divide climb
camps.why: The last low camp with a toilet before the climb to First Divide; ending day one here keeps the 9.7-mile valley walk and leaves the steep ground for the next morning.

camps.name: Home Sweet Home — the meadow camp under First Divide for Steel and Hopper
camps.why: Meadow camp half a mile past First Divide with Steel about a mile away, so the summit is a short day and the walk out starts from the divide side.

camps.name: Camp Pleasant — mid-valley staging on the North Fork Skokomish
camps.why: About 6.5 miles up on easy ground; stop here after a late start, then carry on to Nine Stream or the divide the next day.

plan_conflict: The plan returns to Nine Stream after Steel and walks out from there, but research names Home Sweet Home as the base for Steel, so night 2 is moved there and the walk out is about 13 miles.

camps.name: Ten-Mile Camp
camps.why: Flat, shaded camp with a toilet and bear wire about 10.7 miles in, past Big Hump; it splits the 21-mile approach and is the natural stop on the way back.

camps.name: Marmot Lake — the Duckabush-side high camp for Steel and Duckabush
camps.why: The high camp for Steel on this side: tent sites on a ridge above the lake with water, and a half-day scramble above. It sits at the top of the steep final miles.

camps.name: Upper Duckabush Camp
camps.why: A toilet camp about 3 miles below Marmot Lake; use it to shorten day two or split the final 1,700 ft climb after a late start.

camps.name: Upper Duckabush junction camp — the link between First Divide and the Duckabush head
camps.why: A trail junction camp used by parties crossing from First Divide; on this out-and-back it is not a night, since Upper Duckabush Camp sits on your own route.

camps.name: Nine Stream Camp
camps.why: Nine miles in, with a toilet, just below where the trail starts to climb; leaves the steep haul to First Divide for day two.

camps.name: Home Sweet Home — the meadow camp under First Divide for Steel and Hopper
camps.why: Meadow camp about a mile from Hopper's way-trail start and in reach of the divide, so summit day begins close to the route; the plan's Two Bear camp sits lower down.

camps.name: Camp Pleasant
camps.why: Easy ground about 7 miles in; useful after a late start, but it adds roughly three miles to the next day.

camps.name: Upper Duckabush junction camp — the link between First Divide and the Duckabush head
camps.why: A junction camp on the Duckabush side, well off this route; not slept at on a standard Hopper trip.

plan_conflict: The plan puts night 2 and 3 at Two Bear camp, but research names Home Sweet Home as the camp for Hopper and Steel, so it is the main for nights 2 and 3.

camps.name: 10-Mile Camp
camps.why: First-night camp about 10.8 miles in, past Big Hump, with a toilet and bear wire; breaks the long approach into two days.

camps.name: Marmot Lake — the Duckabush-side high camp for Steel and Duckabush
camps.why: Tent sites on a ridge above the lake look straight at Duckabush, so the off-trail summit day starts at your door. Close to O'Neil Pass at the end of the steep miles.

camps.name: Upper Duckabush Camp
camps.why: A toilet camp about 3 miles below Marmot Lake; stop here if the day-two climb looks too long, then carry up the next morning.

camps.name: Flapjack Lakes — the base camp for the whole Sawtooth Ridge
camps.why: Designated sites with a toilet and water; the only camp the park lists here, with every Sawtooth route a short climb away.

camps.name: Black and White Lakes — the fallback when Flapjack is booked out
camps.why: Higher and quieter, about 1,300 feet above the lakes; use it when Flapjack sites are full, at the cost of extra distance to the summit.

plan_conflict: Flapjack Lakes and Black and White Lakes both carry main on file; research puts parties at Flapjack, so Black and White is changed to route.

camps.name: Lake of the Angels
camps.why: The cirque camp with Skokomish straight above; sleeping here turns the steep trail into a half day in, and the summit push into a day with a light pack.

camps.name: Hamma Hamma River road campgrounds — Lena Creek and Hamma Hamma
camps.why: A drive-in night at the road before the early start; it adds nothing the lake camp gives, only an easier arrival after a long drive.

new_camps.name: Flapjack Lakes
new_camps.why: The one designated camp below Sawtooth Pass, with a toilet and water; sleeping here makes the Fin a half-day climb plus the walk out.
new_camps.water: Water is available from Flapjack Lakes and nearby streams.
new_camps.permit: A wilderness permit is required; camp in designated sites only.
new_camps.notes: About 7.5 miles from the Staircase trailhead. Bear canisters are required and campfires are banned above 3,500 feet.

new_camps.name: Warm Lake camp
new_camps.why: Open meadow sites on the lake's west side put the Klickton Divide face two hours from camp, and the second day leaves time for the long walk out.
new_camps.water: The lake and a creek in the meadows below it.
new_camps.notes: Reached by a bootpath off the Surprise Lake trail; elevation is approximate, contoured from a 6,200 ft level spot. Camp at least 100 feet from the shore.

camps.name: Conrad Meadows and Surprise Lake, South Fork Tieton
camps.why: Wooded, sheltered camp 6.5 miles in; closer to the trailhead than Warm Lake, with the summit push across the basin the next day.

plan_conflict: The plan offers Surprise Lake or Warm Lake; research confirms Warm Lake as the usual overnight for Gilbert's other route, but no source states where Meade Glacier parties sleep.

camps.name: Snowgrass Flat area backcountry camps
camps.why: Legal sites in the timber below the closed flat, about 4 miles from the road; Old Snowy, Ives and Gilbert are all one long day from here.

camps.name: Chambers Lake Campground
camps.why: A drive-in base a mile from the trailheads; fine for the night before, but it adds the four-mile carry to the timber sites.

camps.name: Snowgrass Flat area backcountry camps
camps.why: Legal sites in the timber and on the benches below the closed flat; Old Snowy and Ives are a long day from here, with water close by.

camps.name: Chambers Lake Campground
camps.why: A drive-in base a mile from the trailheads; good for the night before an early start, but it adds the four-mile carry to the timber sites.

plan_conflict: The plan camps in the upper basin near the PCT at 7,100-7,200 ft, but camping is prohibited in Snowgrass Flat and within 100 feet of the PCT, so the established sites below the flat are the main.
